+++ modified
@@ -0,0 +1,29 @@
+---
+assignees:
+- claude-code
+position_column: todo
+position_ordinal: ffa780
+title: 'dead-code goes objective: tool rules supersede the prompt rule; staged work must be annotated'
+---
+Correction to ^teemmch. That card preserved the `dead-code` prompt rule and its judgment. The goal is the opposite: eliminate the judgment with objectivity. The only subjective carve-out — work-in-process scaffolding — becomes an annotation contract: staged code carries the language's own suppression marker, or it is dead. Every other carve-out is already a machine fact the tools understand natively: the Rust compiler exempts `pub` items, `#[cfg(test)]`, and `main` from `dead_code` by itself; staticcheck U1000 exempts exported Go items; the prompt rule exempted the same things by prose.
+
+Per language:
+
+- Rust — new `dead-code-rust`, workspace scope: `cargo check --message-format=json` piped through jq selecting the `dead_code` lint code. `supersedes: dead-code`. Suppression: `#[expect(dead_code, reason = "...")]` — that attribute IS the staging contract; unannotated staged work is a finding. State this in the rule body.
+- Go — promote the existing `unused-code-go` to `supersedes: dead-code`. Suppression: `//lint:ignore U1000 <reason>`. Same contract, stated in the body.
+- TypeScript/JavaScript — new `dead-code-typescript`, files scope: eslint `no-unused-vars` (and the @typescript-eslint variant) via a temporary flat config. Exported symbols are exempt by the rule's nature, the same surface the prompt carve-out exempted. Suppression: `// eslint-disable-next-line no-unused-vars` with a reason.
+- Python — stays on the prompt fallback, and record why in the rule body: vulture below confidence 100 guesses from names (framework overrides, string-referenced attributes), so no objective tool exists for unused Python symbols. `unreachable-code-python` keeps its narrow 100-confidence slice.
+
+Cover the gap superseding creates:
+
+- Orphaned modules: an unwired `.rs` file is never compiled, so the compiler cannot call it dead — and the prompt rule used to catch it. Add a deterministic check to `dead-code-rust`'s run script (or a sibling files-scope rule): a changed `.rs` file that is not `lib.rs`/`main.rs`/`mod.rs`/a `#[path]` target must be named by a `mod` declaration somewhere in its crate. Grep answers this; no judgment.
+
+Documentation moves in the same change:
+
+- Rewrite `dead-code.md` down to what it now is: the fallback for languages without an objective tool, and state the annotation contract.
+- Amend `builtin/validators/README.md`: add the annotation contract to the rules-for-tool-rules section — an exemption a human would argue in prose must instead be an inline suppression the tool reads; staging is the canonical example.
+- Update the code-hygiene VALIDATOR.md dead-code record: the ^teemmch "do not supersede" decision is reversed and why.
+
+Fixture pairs for each new rule; the fail fixture holds an unannotated dead item, the pass fixture holds the same item with the suppression attribute and a reason. Extend `SHIPPED_DEAD_CODE_RULES` and its acceptance test.
+
+#tool-validators
\ No newline at end of file
